I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out with my girlfriend anyway. When I came home, my younger brother had told my mom about the "fight" we had. My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do whatever my sister says because she's "in charge." I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it. I ended up getting grounded for disobeying my sister, who is acting like a pseudo-parent while they're away. I dropped it because I don't want to argue with my mom anymore. I'm wondering if I did the right thing by going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's orders. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? I also found out later that my brother was the one who told my mom, and I forgave him because I can't be mad at him for too long. So, to break it down, my sister was given authority by my parents to be in charge. She tried to stop me from going out, but I didn't listen. My brother told my mom about it, leading to me getting grounded. I'm questioning whether my actions were right or wrong. First, I need to consider the rules set by my parents. They left my sister in charge, which implies that she has the authority to make decisions while they're away. By not listening to her, I was essentially disobeying my parents' instructions. However, I also have my own judgment and freedom, especially since I'm almost an adult. I also need to think about the consequences of my actions. Going out with my girlfriend led to a conflict with my sister, which then resulted in me being grounded. My brother's involvement made things worse because he told my mom, which escalated the situation. On the other hand, I felt that my sister was overstepping her boundaries by trying to control me. She can manage my little brother, but I'm older and closer in age to her. I might have felt that her authority shouldn't extend to me in the same way. I also need to consider the dynamics between me and my sister. If she tends to abuse her power or make unreasonable demands, that could justify my decision to not follow her orders. However, if she was just trying to maintain order and ensure everyone's safety, then maybe I should have respected her authority. Another aspect is the impact on my relationship with my parents. By getting grounded, I'm facing the consequences of my actions, which might teach me a lesson about respecting the hierarchy and rules set by my parents. It's also important to communicate with my sister to clarify the boundaries and expectations to avoid future conflicts. In summary, I need to weigh the importance of respecting the authority given to my sister by my parents against my own judgment and freedom.
